translations.text: Joshua son of Nun sent two men familiar with the land from Shittim and told them, “Go and inspect the land of Jericho.” They went and entered the house of a prostitute named Rahab and spent the night there.

He commanded them, saying, “Take stones for yourselves from here, from the middle of the Jordan, from beneath the priests’ feet. Prepare twelve stones, carry them across with you, and place them where you will spend the night.”
Seven priests shall carry horns and sound them before the ark. On the seventh day, go around the city seven times, and the priests shall blow the horns.
When they sound the horns and you hear the sound of the horn, all the people shall give a great shout. The city wall will fall where it stands, and the people shall go up, each straight ahead.

As Joshua had told the people, seven priests were carrying seven horns and sounding them before the ark of the Lord. They were blowing the horns, and the ark of the Lord’s covenant was following them.
Joshua tore his clothes and fell facedown on the ground before the ark of the Lord until evening, he and the elders of Israel. They put dust on their heads.
They took them from his tent and brought them to Joshua and to all Israel, and he placed them before the Lord.
They raised a heap of large stones over him, which remains to this day. The Lord turned from his fierce anger. Therefore that place has been called the Valley of Achor to this day.
All the warriors who were with him went up and approached the city. They camped north of Ai, with a valley between them and Ai.
Not a man remained in Ai or Bethel who did not go out after Israel. They left the city open and pursued Israel.

The men of Ai turned around and saw the smoke of their city rising to the sky. They were unable to flee in either direction, and the people of Israel, who had been fleeing into the wilderness, turned against their pursuers.
The Israelites said to the Hivites, “If you live among us, why should you receive a pledge from us?”
Our elders and all the inhabitants of our land told us, “Take provisions for the journey and go to meet them. Tell them, ‘We are your servants. Now give us a pledge.’”
Joshua summoned them and said to them, “Why did you deceive us and tell us, ‘We are very far from you,’ when you actually live among us?”

When Joshua and the Israelites had finished inflicting a great slaughter on them, until they were destroyed and not a survivor remained among them, they brought those rebels of Gibeon into their fortified city.
They did as Joshua told them and brought the five kings out of the cave to him: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon.
Joshua, with all Israel accompanying him, went from [?] to Libnah and fought against Libnah.
All these kings gathered and camped together by the waters of Merom, preparing to wage war against Israel.
Joshua did to them as the Lord had told him: he destroyed their horses and burned their chariots with fire.
From the mountain that divides and rises toward Seir as far as Gadgad in the valley of Lebanon beneath Mount Hermon, Joshua subdued all their kings and killed them.
And the plain as far as the Sea of Chinnereth on the east, and as far as the sea of the plain, the Salt Sea, east of the road to Beth-jeshimoth, and southward beneath the slopes of the highlands.
One king of Jerusalem; one king of Hebron.
Their territory extended from Mahanaim and included all Bashan, the entire kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the villages of Jair in Bashan—sixty towns.
The Israelites did as the Lord had commanded Moses, and they divided the land.
It passes through Azmon and goes out to the Wadi of Egypt, and the boundary ends to the west. This shall be your southern boundary.
And Adaroth, Beth-dagon, Naamah, and Naqda: sixteen towns with their surrounding lands.
The boundary goes out from Tappuah to the Jordan and runs to the western boundary of the Kanah Valley, ending in the west. This is the inheritance of the tribe of Ephraim according to their clans.

They came before Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders of Israel and said, “The Lord commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brothers, and at the Lord’s command he gave us one among our father’s brothers. Now give us an inheritance among our fathers’ brothers.” Joshua gave them an inheritance and a portion among their father’s brothers.
When the Israelites grew strong, they subjected the Canaanites to tribute, but they did not destroy them.

The descendants of Joseph said, “The hill country and the towns of the Perizzites are not enough for us, because the Canaanites live in the valley land, in Beth-shean and its villages, and in the Valley of Jezreel.”
Joshua said to the house of Joseph, to the descendants of Ephraim and Manasseh, “You are a numerous people and have great strength, but one portion is enough for you.”
From there the boundary passes to Luz, along the southern side of Luz, which is Bethel. The boundary descends to Ataroth-addar, on the hill south of Lower Beth-horon.
It faces north and goes out to En-shemesh, then goes out to Geliloth opposite the ascent of Ramin, and descends to Laban and to Bohan, Reuben’s son.
It passes along the side facing the valley to the north and descends into the valley.
They had in their inheritance Beersheba, Sheba, and Moladah.

The inheritance of the descendants of Simeon came from the allotment of the descendants of Judah, because the portion of the descendants of Judah was too large. The descendants of Simeon therefore received an inheritance from their inheritance.
It turns from Ashdod eastward to the boundary of Chesulloth and Dabathur, goes out to Rabbith, and ascends to Naphia.
The boundary turns west to Aznoth-boz and goes out from there to Hukkok. It meets Zebulun on the south, Asher on the west, and Judah at the Jordan on the east.

These are the inheritances that Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the ancestral families of the tribes of Israel distributed by lot at Shiloh before the Lord, at the entrance of the tent of meeting. They finished dividing the land.
The Israelites gave the Levites these towns and their surrounding lands by lot, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
They gave them Kiriath-arba, named after the father of the giants, which is Hebron in the hill country of Judah, together with the lands surrounding it.

The descendants of Gershon, from the clan of the Levites, received their towns from the half-tribe of Manasseh: Golan in Bashan, a town of refuge for those who had killed someone, with its surrounding lands, and Ashtaroth with its surrounding lands—two towns with their surrounding lands.

The descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh turned back and left the Israelites at Shiloh in the land of Canaan to go to the land of Gilead, the land of their inheritance, which they had received at the Lord’s command through Moses.
For this reason we said, “Let us make a place for ourselves and build an altar for ourselves, not for sacrifice and not for an offering.”
After many days, the Lord gave Israel rest from all their enemies around them, and Joshua was old and advanced in years.
The people said to Joshua, “We will have no other worship; we worship the Lord God alone.”
Joshua said to the people, “You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen for yourselves to serve the Lord.” They said to him, “We are witnesses.”
Israel served the Lord throughout Joshua’s lifetime and throughout the lifetime of the elders who lived on after Joshua and knew the deeds that the Lord had done for Israel.
